summary: This resolution directs the President to withdraw U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran by 30 days after February 28, 2026, unless Congress enacts a declaration of war or specific authorization for military force.

scores.thoughts: The bill addresses congressional authorization for military hostilities under the War Powers Resolution but contains no provisions, findings, or directives related to funding levels, appropriations, or government expenditures. It focuses solely on the deployment and removal of forces.
No references to taxes, tax policy, revenue measures, or fiscal mechanisms appear in the bill text.
The legislation concerns military engagement with Iran and has no connection to healthcare policy, coverage, or systems.
No content relates to firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.
The bill makes no mention of immigration, borders, visas, or related policies.
No provisions or language address reproductive rights or abortion access.

The bill directs removal of U.S. forces from hostilities against Iran and explicitly preserves defensive capabilities and non-hostile presence. While it constrains offensive military action, it does not address funding, budgets, or spending levels for defense.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related provisions are present.
The resolution contains nothing related to welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
No education policy, schools, or federal involvement in schooling is addressed.
The bill does not engage with drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance policy.
No provisions touch on sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reform.
The text has no bearing on trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
While limiting hostilities could theoretically affect future expenditures, the bill itself makes no reference to deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No language addresses LGBTQ+ protections or related civil rights.
The bill concerns U.S. Armed Forces deployment and does not mention foreign aid, assistance programs, or international funding.
No election integrity, voting access, or electoral provisions are included.
The resolution does not address technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance policy.
No content relates to workers' rights, unions, or labor policy.
The bill contains no provisions on religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination measures.
